exceptions.reason: Spec 8.3's replacement glyph. No bundled face maps a Hebrew or Arabic scalar, so revision 1 shapes each as the deterministic basic-Latin ? from Liberation Sans and reports it as font.missing-glyph, and shapes the trailing paragraph separator U+2029 the same way (decided on #124 and #125). The official export has no bundled glyph for them either and falls through to the pinned container's system fonts: FreeSans for Hebrew in Excalifont text and the system Liberation Sans for Hebrew in Helvetica text, FreeSerif for Arabic in both, and FreeSans's blank advance for the separator. The divergence is each right-to-left cell against its ? glyphs and, on the same line, the Latin word or punctuation the differing advances displace toward the line's unanchored side; the anchored side agrees pixel for pixel (the leading words of the left-aligned lines, the trailing words of the right-aligned lines, the centres of the centred lines), so the visual run order, the digits placed before the Arabic run, the exclamation mark after the Hebrew run and the mirrored bracket pair, matches the official export. The Latin words differ only by the sub-pixel glyph-coverage class recorded on #104, #105, #108, #110, #153 and #169. With #169 the renderer snaps each line's baseline to the device pixel grid as the canvas does; what remains is the two rasterizers' coverage of identically placed outlines and, for the Helvetica-family lines, the reference profile's light autohinting of the container's system Liberation Sans, whose x-height it snaps to the pixel grid (spec 8.5).

purpose: Lay out bidirectional text as spec 8.3 requires, in Excalifont and in Helvetica (fontFamily 2, shaped by Liberation Sans): two centred right-to-left elements whose lines are one Hebrew and one Arabic word, and three left-to-right elements at textAlign left and right whose lines embed an Arabic run followed by European digits (which take the Arabic-number level and precede the run visually), a Hebrew run followed by an exclamation mark, and a Hebrew run holding a bracket pair whose parentheses resolve to the run's level and show their mirror glyphs; one line ends in the paragraph separator U+2029. No bundled face maps a Hebrew or Arabic scalar, so every right-to-left run is spec 8.3's deterministic basic-Latin ? from Liberation Sans, one font.missing-glyph per scalar per occurrence in logical order, and the separator is that replacement glyph too (#125); the official export draws the pinned container's system-font fallback for the same scalars (FreeSans and the system Liberation Sans for Hebrew, FreeSerif for Arabic) and FreeSans's blank for the separator. The right-to-left elements are centred and every element's lines begin in one direction because the harness rasterizer resolves the official export's text-anchor without regard to its direction and the official export anchors every right-to-left element with text-anchor end (#168), and because the reference detects the base direction once per element (#166); left- and right-aligned right-to-left elements and direction-mixed elements are evidenced once those are decided.
